# R401 — decode hardware ceiling and next measurements

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only research on B570 10 GiB / Ryzen 5 5600X / 128 GiB RAM, with user-supplied measured host-to-GPU rate of about 6 GB/s. Canonical source target: `8b48d17c99b70d32781f9f5b056602a598a37b1c` at `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-strata-upstream-sync-skill-20261013`. Reviewed AGENTS.md and `docs/ARTIFACT_RETENTION.md`. No implementation, build, test, benchmark, model, GPU, profiler, service, Git mutation, or cleanup was performed. Did not read the forbidden contract record or scan environment variables. Only this report was written.

## Decision

The measured 70 token/s goal is 8.75× the latest long-context no-MTP decode rates (7.8–8.7 token/s in the task's matched comparison). A token at 70/s has 14.29 ms total wall budget. There is no defensible single hardware roofline today: existing phase timers are nested/overlapping, route counts are not joined to format and residency per request, CPU packed bytes are logical source extent rather than physical DRAM reads, and H2D byte/time by generated token is absent. It is not justified to call the target impossible or to promise a cache/kernel speedup.

A hard conditional H2D envelope is possible from the supplied 6 GB/s: even if all 14.29 ms were transfer time, no more than 85.7 MB (decimal) could be transferred per emitted token. Real allowable H2D traffic must be lower by whatever attention, expert compute, synchronization, sampling, and commit consume. This is a limiting equation, not a claim that decode currently transfers that much or that this link is on the decode critical path.

## Measured state and limits

Task-provided unchanged upstream `bench.sh` result: 32,049 actual input tokens, 24 output tokens, IQ3_S Qwen3.8 FlashNext native packs, top-10 of 512 experts/layer, no MTP. Source `410904c` had COPY0 median 407.5 prefill / 8.6 decode token/s and COPY1 474.8 / 8.7; copy-only queue did not improve decode materially. Later canonical phase-cache comparison: OFF 384.8 / 7.8 and ON 375.4 / 8.2; decode distributions overlap, so phase cache was not adopted as a decode win. The registry-v193 audit reports 948 research entries. The committed official baseline at `bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-phase-off-control/upstream/results.json` independently records the OFF long row as three 32,049-token prompts and 24 generated each, decode 7.3/7.8/8.6 (median 7.8); the same stock file records 4K/16K rows with broad short-output rate variation. Treat the task's paired comparison as the relevant anchor; one 3-sample suite is not a tight estimate of steady-state decode variance.

R314's closed native decode diagnostic is useful to choose instrumentation, not a performance baseline: 16 one-token windows averaged 124.09 ms/window = verify 121.44 (GPU-reach wait 50.27 + per-layer host 55.16 [plan 0.05, actq 0.07, jobs 0.04, CPU 50.64] + stage 0.49) + commit/emit 2.65. Per layer-window it reported 9.45 CPU experts, 0.55 VRAM hits, and zero PCIe experts. The receipt explicitly labels this validation-overhead diagnostic and performance-ineligible. These figures are nested host observations; the 50.27 ms wait can include GPU work, and the 55.16 ms host envelope includes the 50.64 CPU subtotal. Do not add them or scale CPU time by 48/9.45. It has no route-format/NT histogram or physical bandwidth data.

R369v2 audited `native_experts.txt`: one expert's blob over 48 layers is 98,227,200 B; top-10 across all layers is 982,272,000 B (936.77 MiB) if every routed expert is sourced. At 70 tokens/s that logical extent is 68.76 GB/s. This is not DDR traffic or a feasibility bound: cache hits, mapped-file page reuse, repeated route IDs and actual memory-controller reads were not measured. It should not be compared directly with a theoretical RAM bandwidth.

R371v2 resolves the current CPU dispatch shape: no-MTP/spec=0 one-token dispatch has NT=1 per unique top-10 expert. Do not apply NT5–8 grouped-kernel results to this workload. Its candidate CPU paired IQ3_S GU flag saves one repeated logical 2,920-byte Q8_K activation traversal per row pair (1,868,800 B across 640 rows/expert) but those reads may reside in cache; no DRAM saving follows. R314 updates its result: fixture parity passed in free and contrib-LLVM, synthetic single-thread NT1 paired path was 3.76% faster, NT8 was 2.31% slower; no production model arm or type21/NT1 request denominator exists. It remains default-off and is a low-priority, gated test.

## Source-derived critical path and unresolved hardware limits

Canonical source shows native expert jobs are formed from route IDs/provider plans in `src/core/expert_source.cpp` (current dispatch/job construction around 1788–1989; routing stats/histogram around 1415–1440 in the R371 audited source). CPU execution phases are separated at `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp:470-503` (GU, intermediate activation quantization, Down); `src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp` dispatches format/NT-specific routes. `src/core/verify.cpp` coordinates route windows, device execution and completion. The broad diagnostics do not yield exclusive CPU cycles or per-format critical-path attribution. GPU expert work, vocabulary head and attention/indexer/QSA are not timed as separate exclusive intervals in the official `bench.sh` throughput samples. Kernel duration, useful GPU occupancy, memory-controller traffic, request-local H2D bytes, CPU per-worker active/claim/wait time and CPU/GPU overlap therefore remain unmeasured for this exact run.

The task's 6 GB/s host-to-GPU number is an end-to-end link measurement, not evidence of current decode utilization. In the R314 diagnostic, PCIe expert count was zero; do not impute the user-supplied link rate as a decode limiter from prefill copies. Current CPU misses are host-computed; VRAM-hit and CPU ownership are distinct from cache-fill transfers. The older short-context IQ3_S 18.3 token/s measurement included MTP, context 512, warmup and only 128 output tokens; it cannot substitute for the 32K no-MTP anchor. The 29.7 Q2_0 result is a different quant/model path.

## Ranked candidates

1. **First: get a closed, low-observer-cost per-request attribution on the official 32K+ decode.** Aggregate per generated token and per layer: routed IDs, source/provider ownership, GU/Down native types, actual NT, expert blob bytes, VRAM hits/misses, CPU jobs, host-to-device bytes, copy submit/completion time, compute event duration and wait location. Retain only counters/histograms, no route trace. Measure clean throughput separately with instrumentation disabled. This is the highest-value step because it identifies whether the limiting work is CPU expert service, GPU attention/head, cache/mapping, transfer, or synchronization. Do not use aggregate diagnostic `CPU experts` or timer sums as a substitute.

2. **If and only if CPU-owned IQ3_S NT1 GU is material, test the existing paired-GU opt-in.** Current candidate is already parity-qualified at kernel level; no new kernel import is needed. Run 3+ interleaved fresh processes per arm at same 32K input IDs, 128 generated tokens, no MTP, cache/profile/residency, worker/task/affinity and copy policy. Compare clean request decode rate and output IDs/logprob fingerprints; collect the type21/NT1 denominator from the separate bounded diagnostic. Promote only on a repeatable end-to-end gain outside run spread. The 3.76% synthetic component result cannot promise model gain.

3. **If CPU pool dominates after route histogram, test one task-grain axis only.** R314 suggests (after Main closes its long decode measurement) tasks 6/18/24 with worker count fixed, interleaved fresh 32K+128 runs. This is not yet measured for the current 128-token reference. Record completion and wait per worker only in a separate diagnostic. Avoid repeating worker-count screens or conflating more fragments with more participating threads.

4. **If route-locality and cache-fill bytes are material, evaluate cache admission/reuse from actual routes before changing eviction policy.** Use bounded per-layer hit/miss and byte-weighted reuse histograms; compare current static/profile ordering with independent LRU3/LRU19 simulations on held-out requests. Only then consider a guarded adaptive cache. Existing phase-cache OFF/ON decode results do not support adopting phase caching for speed. R369 route-union bounds and static top-19 counts are logical only. Any live policy change must preserve source snapshot, queued-copy completion, graph/reader retirement, cache leases, and failure cleanup.

5. **Only if event timings show a discrete GPU kernel bound, investigate GPU dispatch/fusion.** Current decode has one token, so prefill grouped GEMM, multi-token batching, and NT5–8 weight-decode amortization do not transfer. Isolate QSA/indexer, attention, routed GPU expert, head, token sampling and synchronization with device events and host wait spans. A fused quantized matvec/activation/route-combine path is a plausible architecture class, but no current source evidence proves which fusion saves critical-path time or fits 10 GiB. Do not port a vLLM/SGLang batched EP kernel to this one-token SYCL route without a matching layout and launch-count profile.

## External implementation check (primary sources)

- llama.cpp's official [`--cpu-moe` implementation/options](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md) establish CPU expert placement as a neighboring design, but do not prove a temporal GPU cache or Ryzen speedup. Its [backend selective expert copy discussion](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/20757) is an open proposal, not merged implementation evidence. The persistent cache proposals [#24528](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/24528) and [#28248](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions/28248) contain contributor-reported results and are not independent benchmarks or primary code results.
- vLLM's official [fused MoE kernel feature guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md) and [modular kernel design](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/fused_moe_modular_kernel.md) describe batched expert tokens, quantization-specific kernels and dispatch/finalize interfaces. These target accelerator batch/EP serving and do not establish value for Strata's one-token, CPU/GPU mixed route.
- SGLang's [expert parallelism docs](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/advanced_features/expert_parallelism.mdx) describe dispatch/combine, grouped GEMM and EPLB using observed activation statistics. That is a multi-device load-balance architecture, not single-card cache admission evidence.
- Intel's [`llm-scaler`](https://github.com/intel/llm-scaler) is an XPU-focused vLLM serving project; its codebase is useful for hardware-specific comparator research but no directly comparable B570 IQ3_S one-token CPU offload result was located in this pass.
- A personal [MoE hot-cache proposal](https://github.com/ap03906101/moe-hotcache) and llama.cpp cache RFCs raise slot lifetime/quarantine concerns; author claims are not independent evidence. Transfer only the need to prove readers/copy completion before reuse, already reflected in Strata's publication/cache ownership rules.

These sources point toward measured route-aware admission and narrow kernel selection, but none provides a transferable numeric roofline. No external speedup was used.

## Concrete Main measurement sequence

A. Preserve the official unchanged `bench.sh` 32,049/24 control and latest 32K+128 no-MTP worker run as separate workload definitions. Report individual samples, actual generated tokens, output identity, commit/source/build hashes, settings, and normal close/fault outcome. Do not call the 24-token stock row sustained decode.

B. Run a diagnostic-only paired 32K+128 request with bounded aggregate counters: per-layer route count/type/provider/hit/miss/packed bytes, H2D bytes and copy event timing, CPU phase by GU/quant/Down plus actual NT, and GPU event timing for attention/indexer, GPU expert, head, sample/commit. Add explicit wait intervals and overlap boundaries. No per-iteration logs; keep collection within a stated size budget. Compare its aggregate rates only as instrumentation sanity, not performance.

C. Produce a critical-path timeline from timestamps/events (union of concurrently active CPU/GPU/copy intervals), not a sum of phase timers. For each layer and full token, separate exclusive wall from overlap. Calculate candidate Amdahl bounds only after exclusive attributable fraction `f` and an isolated measured factor `g` exist: `S <= 1 / ((1-f) + f/g)`. Until then neither quantity is known.

D. Use the diagnosed dominant phase to select one axis (paired GU if eligible; pool tasks if CPU scheduling; cache if measured miss/route reuse; kernel fusion if GPU event bound). Interleave at least three clean fresh-process repetitions per arm and keep all remaining settings fixed. Require correctness, exact generated token count/output fingerprint, no fault, normal process close, and a consistent decode endpoint gain before adoption. Retain individual samples under ARTIFACT_RETENTION; no cleanup during a run.

E. For an H2D-limited verdict, report measured bytes/token and exposed transfer time/token; compare against the conditional 85.7 MB/token maximum at 70/s. For a CPU DRAM-limited verdict, obtain actual per-worker memory-controller read/write counters for the timed region and a matched stream-bandwidth baseline under the same CPU/NUMA/memory conditions. For GPU-bound verdict, obtain hardware-supported device counter/event evidence. Nominal link, CPU/GPU theoretical bandwidth and logical packed bytes alone are insufficient.

## Prior evidence reviewed / non-duplication

Reviewed registry v193 and its selected session statements; R371v2 (corrected AVX2/NT1), R383 (quantizer reuse; concludes quantizer already occurs once at correct scopes), R369v2 (corrected route bytes), R314 (measured decode ledger and pool next axis), R311 (superseded paired-GU prior), R342 (upstream `--long` row cap/measurement meaning), R354 (copy-queue host-call audit), and prefill-oriented R396–399 for cache/lifetime constraints. R396–399 discuss layer-major prefill only; they are not decode candidates or evidence for 70/s. The historical paired summary and selected-session statements confirm the short-context and old candidate numbers above. The existing official phase-cache and upstream bench receipts were consulted for the supplied baseline. No new measurements or source conclusions were inferred from their status labels alone.
